newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BASF sets up headquarters in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: BASF sets up headquarters in Singapore.

text.p: German chemical conglomerate BASF plans to relocate the headquarters of its textile and leather dyes and chemicals division from Germany to Singapore on October 1, the company said on Thursday.

Albert Muller, president of the new BASF Textile and Leather Dyes and Chemicals Pte Ltd, said in a statement Singapore was chosen because "it gives best accessibility to the Asian markets in terms of shipping and communication".
The Singapore office would give BASF quick and easy access to its busiest markets in Asia, namely Japan, Taiwan, Korea, China and India, the statement said.
BASF said Asia, which has the fastest growing textile and leather market in the world, accounts for 30 percent of BASF's sales in these products.
The textile dyes division contributed 2 billion German marks (US$1.4 billion) to the company's worldwide sales of 46.2 billion marks in 1995.
BASF also said it will establish a textile and leather development and application centre in Pasir Gudang, Malaysia, which will be completed by March 1997.
